_comment: The builds of 0G's broker image (ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker) that a
provider may run. The per-service compose baseline (brokercompose.json) lets the
three services that run this image move between digests without a gateway release;
this file is what they may move TO. A service under the baseline's `repository` rule
matches only when its digest is listed here.
AN ACCEPTANCE LIST, NOT A MIRROR OF THE REGISTRY. On 2026-10-15 ghcr.io carried 20
v* tags for this repository. Two of them are running on mainnet providers and are
deliberately NOT listed: v0.5.1 (sha256:ec5df834…, cn-20) and v0.5.2
(sha256:9d0ae9b9…, cn-19). v0.5.4 is the first release the broker team reports as
carrying #759 — the controller may create no new container unless the compose sets
ZG_CONTROLLER_ENGINES=on, and may swap an image only as repo@digest after recording
the swap in RTMR3 — and #763, which lets broker-ingress drop /var/run/dstack.sock,
the socket whose EmitEvent would let any holder append forged RTMR3 records.
Accepting an older build accepts a controller without those constraints. Two further
fleet digests (sha256:c5126640…, cn-1/cn-4/cn-41; sha256:75a2098d…, cn-39/cn-40) are
not pointed at by any v* tag at all.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS WORTH depends on where its digest came from, and the digest alone
cannot show that — which is why `verified` is required on every entry. Resolve the
release TAG against the registry; never copy a digest off a running provider, since
the provider's digest is the thing being checked. To resolve a tag anonymously:
T=$(curl -s 'https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker:pull' | jq -r .token)
curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" \
-H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' \
https://ghcr.io/v2/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker/manifests/<tag> | grep -i docker-content-digest
A tag can be moved after the fact, so record the date the tag was resolved. Where the
release carries signed provenance, verify it with cosign before relying on it, and say
in `verified` whether that was done.
AN EMPTY `releases` LIST accepts nothing: every service under a `repository` rule
then mismatches, with a reason that names this file. It never means 'any digest'.
Fields: `repository` is the bare image repository. Each release has `version` (for
reports only — never compared), `digest` (sha256: and 64 lowercase hex, compared
exactly), and `verified` (the audit trail; never read by code).

verified: 2026-10-15: ghcr.io tag v0.5.4 resolved to this digest (anonymous pull token; HEAD /v2/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker/manifests/v0.5.4, Docker-Content-Digest).
2026-10-15: an OCI referrer is attached via tag sha256-951f4c79…: a Sigstore bundle v0.3 (DSSE envelope) with predicateType https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1, created 2026-10-14T10:53:06Z.

NOT verified here: the bundle's signature and signer identity — the environment that recorded this entry had no cosign. Run cosign verify-attestation against the broker repository's release workflow identity before relying on the provenance.
Corroborated by: the broker team's v0.5.4 release announcement, and the testnet provider 0x1cB95Eb66Cc67C62d4DE0CC96726C5A5d82e7C85 running this digest in all three broker services.
